title: Quillworks uplift scoping and regional activation planning
summary: Follow-up on contract renewal window, scope for capacity uplift, and phased activation of EU + APAC geoclusters. Scoped technical requirements for VPC private plane, KMS integration, and throughput SLOs; agreed to run a 48-hour latency & cost benchmark on sample traffic and deliver a priced addendum for the uplift.
topics: private deployment / VPC networking and KMS
next_steps: Redwood to send priced addendum and sample SOW by 2026-09-18
SE to run 48-hour latency + cost benchmarks with Quillworks sample by 2026-09-21
Customer to confirm internal approvers and procurement timeline by 2026-09-20
Schedule deep-dive on VPC peering and firewall rules week of 2026-09-21
action_items: Devon Park - run throughput and p50/p95 latency tests using Quillworks replay by 2026-09-21
Maya Zhang - compile SOC2 + network diagram and share with Priya by 2026-09-18
Liam O'Connor - provide 48-hour production traffic sample and token distribution by 2026-09-16
Elena Rodriguez - prepare pricing addendum and draft renewal calendar by 2026-09-18
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-14 15:00 UTC | Duration approx 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Elena Rodriguez (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Zhang (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Quillworks CTO), Priya Singh (Quillworks Head of Platform), Marcus Lee (Quillworks DevOps), Sofia Alvarez (Product)

Summary: quick follow-up to the renewal notice and scoping for additional capacity and regions. Ran through technical constraints and next steps.

[00:00] Elena: All right everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll run about 45 minutes, quick agenda — renewal window, sizing uplift, EU then APAC activation, and technical pre-reqs for private plane — VPC, KMS, SSO.
[00:18] Liam: Sounds good. High level from our side: we want to lock renewal by end of month, ideally get EU online before Black Friday, and APAC in Q1. Need clarity on cost and the activation timeline.
[00:34] Elena: Great. Devon, can you cover the sizing guidance?
[00:38] Devon: Yeah. So current baseline you sent — thanks — shows peak concurrent of about 220 requests, distribution heavy on short chat calls that average 180 tokens. For predictable latency we'd recommend moving from your current reserved tier X to mid-tier Y and add two EU geocluster nodes. That gets you p95 latency around 180–210ms on 2k token sequences, and cost increases roughly 1.6x on token basis but we should offset with batching / cache.
[01:02] Priya: Wait, 1.6x is on the token bill, is that inclusive of the burst nodes or just base? Want to make sure we understand fixed vs variable.
[01:10] Devon: That's a blended estimate — base reserved capacity plus expected burst. We'll break out fixed reserved monthly and expected overage.
[01:18] Sofia: Also, we have strict data residency rules in EU. Do we need Private (VPC) or is hosted with residency controls OK?
[01:27] Maya: Good question. For Quillworks, if data at rest in EU is required, our Private offering or VPC-hosted private plane is the usual. Hosted API can give region routing and retention controls, but not same isolation guarantees as dedicated VPC.
[01:41] Marcus: If we do VPC, what's the networking work? We are on AWS, so is it simple peering?
[01:47] Devon: Typical is VPC peering or Transit Gateway. We do require certain firewall rules and egress to Redwood-managed subnets. We'll share the network diagram. It's usually a one-week setup from customer network side if they have infra ready.
[02:02] Liam: KMS — can you do customer-managed keys?
[02:05] Elena: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integration for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we have managed KMS with options for bring-your-own-key via our enterprise package.
[02:14] Priya: Okay. timeline — if we sign renewal by Sept 30, what are realistic activation dates?
[02:19] Devon: Rough plan: final SOW and addendum by Sept 18, benchmark run 48 hours Sept 20–21, network setup Sept 22–29, EU activation in staging Oct 6, production cutover Oct 20. APAC would be a separate activation in Q1.
[02:36] Liam: That EU production Oct 20 is tight — we were aiming for early November. Is Oct 20 optimistic?
[02:42] Devon: It is aggressive; it's dependent on network handoff and your procurement signoff. We can plan for Nov 5 as buffer.
[02:49] Priya: Procurement — our legal needs the SLA language and audit logs sample.
[02:53] Maya: We'll send the SLA excerpt and sample audit log format. Also SOC2 report.
[03:00] Elena: I'll put those in the addendum packet.
[03:05] [03:15] Liam: About the benchmarks, what exactly will you run in the 48-hour test?
[03:18] Devon: We'll run a replay of your sample traffic with token distribution you provide, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tail behavior with KV cache cold vs warm, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also test fallbacks — if EU capacity saturated we route to hosted fallback in nearby region and measure latency delta.
[03:37] Marcus: Will that require us to share real user data? We prefer synthetic but representative.
[03:41] Devon: Synthetic replay is fine as long as distribution matches. Real PII not required; you can sanitize. The key is sequence length and concurrency shape.
[03:50] Sofia: On the cost note, can Redwood recommend quantization or model variant to reduce cost for short chat use cases?
[03:56] Devon: Yes, we can recommend a quantized variant with similar output quality or suggest an ensembled routing policy — short chats to cheaper variant, longer sequences to high-quality model. We'll include model routing recommendations in the addendum.
[04:08] [04:25] Liam: Competitors — we've been talking to Anthropic and looking at Bedrock. How do you stack on deterministic latency and private deployments?
[04:33] Elena: Our differentiation: production-grade telemetry with token-level cost and tracing, plus a unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so rollouts are consistent. Bedrock has broad infra but not the same turnkey private plane; Anthropic's offering has different primitives. We'll include a succinct comparison.
[04:50] Priya: Procurement question — do you do monthly invoicing or net-30?
[04:53] Elena: Standard is net-30, can discuss quarterly invoicing for committed capacity.
[04:57] [05:10] Marcus: Firewalls — we need a list of CIDRs and TLS requirements.
[05:13] Devon: We'll send a network appendix with CIDRs, expected ports (443 outbound + a few control ports), and TLS v1.2+ requirements.
[05:22] Sofia: Any role-based controls for team access? We need RBAC and SSO.
[05:26] Maya: Yes, RBAC with SSO (SAML / OIDC), audit logs and token-level attribution. We'll share a quickstart for SSO setup.
[05:36] [06:00] Liam: On billing — if we grow faster than forecast, can we add burst capacity?
[06:04] Elena: Yes, there are burst policies. We can provision burst pools for weekends or spikes; they have a different rate. We'll include options in the addendum.
[06:12] Priya: For the pilot, do we need a separate contract?
[06:15] Elena: We usually do a short-term pilot addendum under the master subscription, yes 30 days with rollback and metrics gating.
[06:23] Devon: Technical note: for EU private we recommend enabling prefix/KV cache warmup scripts before traffic peaks to reduce first-token latency. We'll provide a small SDK hook for that.
[06:35] [06:50] Marcus: Are there any runtime kernel constraints for our model family? We run a trimmed LLM fork that has longer context.
[06:56] Devon: We support long-context variants; runtime picks optimized kernels. For extreme contexts >8k we may need different instance types; we'll surface that in the benchmark.
[07:08] Liam: Good. Let's talk procurement path: who signs?
[07:12] Sofia: For us, CTO + Legal sign for renewal under current T&Cs, finance needs cost center approval.
[07:18] Elena: We'll include an executive summary for your legal and finance to speed review.
[07:24] [07:40] Priya: Question on logs retention — we need 12 months of audit logs with export capability.
[07:45] Maya: We can configure audit retention and exports; 12 months is supported as an add-on.
[07:50] Devon: One more thing on fallback routing: we can set a policy that keeps latency SLOs by routing partial traffic to hosted variants if private capacity reaches 90%. That ensures availability but may change cost.
[08:05] Liam: Ok, we like that. Can you show a concrete example of cost delta for routing 20% to hosted?
[08:10] Elena: We'll add a worked example in the addendum based on your sample.
[08:15] [08:30] Marcus: For the benchmark, what telemetry do you need from us?
[08:33] Devon: Just the replay file, sequence tokens, and a basic mapping of request types. We'll instrument with tracing headers for attribution.
[08:40] Sofia: We'll try to get the sample over by EOD Thursday (that's 2026-09-16).
[08:45] Liam: On the addendum, if we commit to a 12-month reserved uplift, what's the discount?
[08:50] Elena: Ballpark — 12–20% on unit tokens depending on commitment level. Exact numbers in addendum.
[08:57] [09:10] Priya: Any compliance docs for data sovereignty in EU?
[09:14] Maya: We'll send our data flow and residency controls plus SOC2. For Private, all data at rest and logs can remain in customer-controlled VPC.
[09:23] Devon: Note: with customer-managed KMS we do envelope encryption and we never see keys.
[09:30] [09:45] Liam: Let's lock people on next internal checkpoint. When can Redwood present the priced SOW?
[09:49] Elena: Sept 18.
[09:51] Liam: Good.
[09:53] [10:05] (cross-talk) Sofia: procurement needs a sample invoice.
[10:08] Elena: We'll attach a sample invoice format.
[10:12] Devon: Also we'll include model recommendations: quantized variant for short chats, full precision for case generation.
[10:20] [10:40] Priya: Small question — what about SLA credits for latency miss?
[10:44] Maya: SLA credit policy tied to uptime; for latency we have SLOs and playbooks, credits can be negotiated in enterprise contract.
[10:53] Devon: For the pilot we'll capture performance baselines and then gate production activation.
[11:02] [11:25] Liam: Anything else on technical blockers? Marcus: Our egress policies are strict; will monitor.
[11:30] Marcus: We'll also need a runbook template for failover.
[11:34] Devon: We'll provide a failover runbook and test playbook.
[11:40] [11:55] Elena: Ok let's recap — Redwood: addendum + SOW + benchmarks + SOC2 + network diagram by Sept 18; SE benchmark by Sept 21; Quillworks to provide traffic sample by Sept 16 and confirm approvers by Sept 20.
[12:10] Liam: That matches our expectations. If the benchmarks meet p95 targets, we sign the uplift.
[12:17] Elena: Great. Any final questions?
[12:20] Sofia: No, that's it. Thanks.
[12:22] Elena: Thank you all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the network deep-dive and share the docs.
[12:27] (meeting ends)

References/Links: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/quillworks-uplift | benchmark-sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/quillworks-replay | security docs: https://redwood.app/security/soc2

End of transcript.
